hints: Look carefully at the three organs first. The left circle with a star in the middle is a root, the middle circle with separate bundles is a stem, and the flat shape on the right is a leaf midrib.
Remember the position rule: in a root phloem sits between the arms of the xylem, in a stem phloem is outside xylem in each bundle, and in a leaf xylem is on top with phloem underneath.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three plant organs**

First, work out what you are looking at. Left is a transverse section of a root with its central stele. Middle is a transverse section of a stem with six separate vascular bundles. Right is a transverse section through the midrib of a leaf.

This matters because xylem and phloem swap relative positions in different organs.

**Recall where xylem and phloem sit**

Think of this simple pattern. In a root, xylem forms a central cross or star and phloem fills the gaps between the arms. In a stem bundle, xylem is toward the inside and phloem is toward the outside. In a leaf midrib, xylem is uppermost (toward the top of the leaf) and phloem is lowermost.

**Apply the rule to labels 1 to 4**

Label 1 points to the tissue between the xylem arms in the root, so it is phloem. Label 2 points to the outer part of a stem bundle, so it is phloem. Label 4 is the upper tissue in the leaf vein, so it is xylem, and label 3 is the lower tissue, so it is phloem.

That gives 1 phloem, 2 phloem, 3 phloem, 4 xylem, which is row A.

options.A: Correct. 1 is root phloem between xylem arms, 2 is outer stem bundle phloem, 3 is lower leaf phloem and 4 is upper leaf xylem.
options.B: Incorrect. Label 2 is the outer part of the stem bundle, which is phloem not xylem.
options.C: Incorrect. It reverses everything, label 1 is not central xylem and label 4 is not phloem.
options.D: Incorrect. Labels 1 and 2 are both phloem, not xylem, even though 4 as xylem is right.
